title: Yihan Wang, PhD
text:
What I Work On


📋 CMS Claims Data
Large-scale Medicare & Medicaid data — harmonization, linkage, and analytics across millions of beneficiaries.


🔗 Causal Inference
Propensity scoring, instrumental variables, and difference-in-differences to answer real-world treatment questions.


📈 Survival & Longitudinal Analysis
Time-to-event modeling, competing risks, and repeated measures in aging populations.


🤖 Machine Learning (In Progress)
Expanding into gradient boosting, survival ML, and NLP for clinical text — applied to claims and EHR data.


🛠️ Tools
Stata · R · Python (learning) · SQL


🏥 Domain
Geriatrics · ADRD · Emergency & Hospital Visit Outcomes · Health Services Research

title: Yihan Wang, PhD
text:
Featured Projects
Japan Loneliness Study — Stata code and analysis pipeline for a published mediation analysis examining mobile phone use and loneliness among older Japanese adults. Innovation in Aging, 2020.
WTC First Responders Frailty Study (Ongoing) — Lead biostatistician on a clinical study examining frailty trajectories in World Trade Center first responders. Responsible for statistical analysis plan, modeling, and results interpretation.
ADRD Drug Repurposing Study (In Progress) — Lead analyst using large-scale CMS claims data to identify candidate drugs for Alzheimer’s Disease and Related Dementias (ADRD) repurposing. Applying causal inference methods to observational claims data.
Palliative Care at Home RCT (Recruitment Ongoing) — Biostatistician on a randomized controlled trial evaluating a home-based palliative care intervention. Responsible for research database management, consort diagram design, and statistical analysis planning.

title: Yihan Wang, PhD
text:
Currently Learning
I’m actively building toward health data science and applied ML roles — redoing past analyses in Python, working through survival ML methods, and developing explainability skills (SHAP) for clinical model deployment.

Open to roles in health data science, real-world evidence (RWE), and applied ML in clinical settings.

title: About
text:
I’m a senior research scientist in the Brookdale Department of Geriatrics and Palliative Care at Mount Sinai Hospital, where I’ve spent 5+ years working with large-scale CMS Medicare and Medicaid claims data to study aging, ADRD, and emergency and hospital visit outcomes.
My core expertise is in CMS Medicare and Medicaid data — from raw claims ingestion and harmonization through to analysis and results interpretation. I’ve built pipelines and models using Stata and R, applying methods including regression, longitudinal analysis, survival modeling, and causal inference frameworks.
I currently serve as lead biostatistician on a WTC first responders frailty study, lead analyst on an ADRD drug repurposing project using CMS claims, and biostatistician on a randomized controlled trial of a palliative care at home intervention.
I’m currently in a deliberate transition toward health data science and applied machine learning — combining my domain expertise and analytical rigor with modern ML methods. I’m actively building Python skills, exploring gradient boosting and survival ML models, and developing literacy in explainability tools for clinical deployment contexts.
